Downy_Mildew.quote: Shoots showing primary spikes are stunted with shortened internodes and pale green leaves that are brittle.
Cones that are infected become brown, harden and are affected in their development.
This pathogen produces reproductive structures called sporangia that appear as dark, fuzzy, "downy" growth on the underside of the leaves and sometimes on heavily infected cones.
Early spring symptoms include dark brown rootstocks and primary basal spikes (stunted plants with pale and curled leaves), which are characteristic of systemic infection.

Powdery_Mildew.quote: The symptoms first manifest as pale green to yellow spots on the top of the leaves along with white blotches on the stems and cones.
Infected cones exhibit white, powdery growth externally and underneath bracts and bracteoles, and some cones exhibit brown discoloration and stunting.
